facts.text: Tekamah was founded in October 1854 by pioneer Benjamin R., marking the first permanent settlement in what would become Burt County.
The city’s name comes from the Omaha word for 'big cottonwood,' reflecting the region’s historic trees.
Railroad lines, notably the Chicago & North Western, spurred Tekamah’s growth in the late 19th century before the tracks were later removed.
Tekamah’s Carnegie Library, built in 1916, was expanded with a 2013 addition, preserving its historic charm while serving modern patrons.
The Tekamah Auditorium hosts the annual Burt County Cattlemen’s feast, a cultural highlight that draws visitors from across the region.
Each year, residents celebrate a sweet corn festival, showcasing local produce and community spirit in a lively street‑side event.
